mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over a 3-month period indicates growing demand in the economy, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where HOUST increased over a 3-month period.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% over a 3-month period signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage costs and reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE decreased by more than 0.5% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over a 3-month period indicates increased economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 1% month-over-month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5%, it signals strong consumer demand and a tight labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where RSAFS increased by more than 1% MoM and UNRATE was below 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% over a 3-month period signals deflationary pressure, which increases the real value of debt and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where CPIAUCSL decreased by more than 0.5% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 jobs in a single month and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 2%, it signals strong job growth in a low-interest-rate environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200k in 1 month and FEDFUNDS < 2%
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 200k and FEDFUNDS was below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over a 3-month period indicates strong economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where GDPC1 increased over a 3-month period.
